label: lem:zero_deriv_constant
title: Zero derivative implies constant
statement: If $G$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; G\; 0\; x$ for all $x \in (a,b)$, then $G(x) = G(a)$ for all $x \in [a,b]$.
proof: For $x = a$ the result is immediate. For $a < x$, restrict to $[a,x]$ and apply the MVT to get $c \in (a,x)$ with $G'(c) = (G(x) - G(a))/(x-a)$. Since $G'(c) = 0$ and $x \ne a$, we get $G(x) = G(a)$.
